documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Faculty Affairs / CTLE
documents.title: Gen AI and Teaching Guidelines - Faculty
documents.summary: Provost-office guidance for VCU faculty that asks every instructor to put an AI statement in the syllabus and choose whether to prohibit, allow with acknowledgment, or build in AI. It adds considerations for faculty (privacy, FERPA, equity, bias, detector limits) and an optional sample syllabus statement.
documents.stance_why: The guidance says it is "not to set hard" do's and don'ts and that "It is the instructor’s prerogative whether they choose to prohibit its use, allow its use with transparency/acknowledgment by students, or actively include its use", so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors; the suggested statement is optional ("not an official VCU policy").

units.why: The opening says the guidelines aim to "provide guidance and have conversations about AI use" rather than set rules; this states the document's purpose and scope, so it is a framework statement (P56), informs, general.
units.anchor: provide guidance and have conversations about AI use

units.why: "Striking the right balance between technology, such as Gen AI, and teaching and learning can benefit both students and instructors" names a benefit without making a rule, so P87 informs.
units.anchor: can benefit both students and instructors
units.frag_start: Striking the right balance between technology

units.why: "these guidelines may be updated and/or revised accordingly" says the guidance is provisional, so P54 revisit regularly.
units.anchor: these guidelines may be updated and/or revised accordingly

units.why: The sentence says the Faculty Advisory Committee "was formed to deliberate on the fast pace of changes in the AI arena", describing who produces the guidance; P84 (how and by whom the policy was made) fits better than P80 because it is about origin, not enforcement.
units.anchor: was formed to deliberate on the fast pace of changes in the AI arena

units.why: The committee is described as "providing continued guidance, including hands-on workshops and sessions", i.e. support for faculty learning about AI, so P63.
units.anchor: providing continued guidance, including hands-on workshops and sessions

units.anchor: Students may be expected to possess the skills and competencies to effectively utilize Gen AI

units.why: "it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy, as well as remain aware of its potential drawbacks and limitations" recommends AI literacy for the community; closest is P44 (AI use as skill) though it also names limitations.
units.anchor: it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy
units.fit_note: Also asks users to stay aware of AI drawbacks and limitations, which P44 does not capture.

units.why: "we also encourage faculty to continue actively fostering students’ ongoing learning of essential materials, refinement of critical thinking skills" tells instructors to keep students doing their own learning and thinking, nearest to P32 (students stay primary thinker).
units.anchor: refinement of critical thinking skills, and demonstration of applied knowledge
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty as a duty to foster student learning, not to students as a rule.

units.anchor: Supplementary materials will also be added to the Gen AI Resource Tool

documents.title: Generative AI at VCU
documents.summary: Office of the CIO page on generative AI at VCU: licensed tools, data protection, FERPA and FOIA, verification of output, meeting bots, phishing, and IT Governance review of tools. It refers student-use decisions to instructors and the Faculty Affairs syllabus statements.
documents.stance_why: The page mostly sets data, tool-approval and security rules, and says Faculty Affairs "dictate that instructors will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI for their course assignments"; it gives no default stance on student AI use and leaves the decision to instructors.

units.why: The page defines "Generative Artificial Intelligence ... refers to systems that can create new content", which sets what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: refers to systems that can create new content

units.why: "VCU provides Google Gemini, Microsoft CoPilot, and Adobe Firefly through our enterprise licenses" names institution-wide licensed tools, so P92 (not P17, which is course-specific).
units.anchor: VCU provides Google Gemini, Microsoft CoPilot, and Adobe Firefly through our enterprise licenses

units.why: "Do not enter confidential (Category 1) or sensitive (Category 2) data into any AI tools unless they have been approved" is a data-protection rule, so P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter confidential (Category 1) or sensitive (Category 2) data into any AI tools

units.why: "Information given to generative AI tools is not private" states the privacy risk behind the rule, so P50 informs.
units.anchor: Information given to generative AI tools is not private

units.why: "Adhere to current university guidelines and policies when using AI tools" requires compliance with existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: Adhere to current university guidelines and policies when using AI tools

units.why: The "Acceptable Use of Generative AI Technology" policy "establishes requirements and guardrails for safe adoption and usage", so this points to a university-wide framework, P56 informs.
units.anchor: establishes requirements and guardrails for safe adoption and usage of Generative AI tools

units.why: "dictate that instructors will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI for their course assignments" requires instructors to state AI expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI for their course assignments

units.why: "It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted or infringes on the rights of any third party" bans copyrighted inputs, so P52 (copyright) with a fit note since it is a prohibition.
units.anchor: It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted
units.fit_note: A direct ban on uploading copyrighted content, not just a consideration of licensing.

units.why: "the university will continue to update its guidance and policies" says the guidance will keep changing, so P54.
units.anchor: the university will continue to update its guidance and policies
units.frag_start: As the landscape of AI technology evolves

units.why: "Do not upload student work to Generative AI tools without written consent from the student" is a FERPA-based data rule; nearest P50.
units.anchor: Do not upload student work to Generative AI tools without written consent from the student
units.fit_note: FERPA rule on student work, not general data protection.

units.why: "they can be subject to the Freedom of Information Act" says AI chats about VCU business, even on personal accounts, fall under public-records law, so P77 informs.
units.anchor: they can be subject to the Freedom of Information Act

units.why: "You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish" makes users answerable for AI-assisted output, so P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish
units.frag_start: You are responsible for any content

units.why: "AI-generated content can be wrong or misleading" warns of error, so P31 informs.
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be wrong or misleading

units.why: "Check the generated content against reliable sources" tells users to verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Check the generated content against reliable sources

units.why: "Do not trust AI data to give medical, legal, financial advice" warns against reliance on AI output, so P31 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Do not trust AI data to give medical, legal, financial advice
units.fit_note: Limits a type of use (professional advice), beyond verification.

units.why: "Avoid using unauthorized third-party bots with Zoom and Google Meet" restricts AI meeting bots; nearest P86 though it is about vetting, not consent.
units.anchor: Avoid using unauthorized third-party bots with Zoom and Google Meet
units.fit_note: Concerns vetting of meeting bots for confidentiality, not asking participants' consent.

units.why: "VCU has vetted and approved the use of two transcription tools" names approved AI transcription tools, so P92.
units.anchor: VCU has vetted and approved the use of two transcription tools

units.why: "it is recommended to use the built in transcription tool" for Google Meet notes recommends an approved tool, so P92.
units.anchor: it is recommended to use
units.frag_start: For Google Meet, it is recommended to use

units.why: "Learn the terms of service and privacy policies for the public Generative AI system you want to use" asks users to evaluate a tool before use; nearest P117.
units.anchor: Learn the terms of service and privacy policies for the public Generative AI system
units.fit_note: Evaluation is of terms of service and data handling, not accuracy or task fit.

units.why: "Be mindful of any rights the platform may claim over the content you create using their system" raises ownership and licensing, so P52.
units.anchor: Be mindful of any rights the platform may claim over the content you create

units.why: "Generative AI has made it easier for bad actors to create scams on a larger scale" warns of AI-enabled phishing, so P75.
units.anchor: has made it easier for bad actors to create scams on a larger scale
units.frag_start: Generative AI has made it easier

units.why: "Send suspicious messages to infosec@vcu.edu" gives a reporting channel for suspected AI-enabled phishing; P75 fits best since the topic is phishing, with P71 not chosen because it concerns incidents more broadly.
units.anchor: Send suspicious messages to infosec@vcu.edu

units.why: "Any technology that stores, processes, or sends VCU data must have the required privacy, security and accessibility protections and be reviewed" requires IT review of tools, so P65.
units.anchor: must have the required privacy, security and accessibility protections

units.why: "Only use third-party tools that have been vetted and approved by IT Governance" requires use of approved tools, so P92.
units.anchor: Only use third-party tools that have been vetted and approved by IT Governance

units.why: "will need a contract with the vendor and to go through the VCU IT Governance review and approval" sets the approval path for other AI tools, so P65.
units.anchor: will need a contract with the vendor and to go through the
units.frag_start: Other tools not found on this page

notes: Coder A. The collect file notes the Nov 2025 Acceptable Use of Generative AI Technology policy full text was not found. The CTLE text repeats the IP and student-data paragraphs under two headings; repeats coded once. No school, computing or course documents were collected.
